Subject: Briefing request: May 3 tokenization latency spike (customer impact)

Hi Grace,

We saw an elevated tokenization latency and intermittent 503s across several endpoints on May 3 between 02:15–03:05 UTC that affected our high-priority flows. Our SREs captured traces and would like a concise RCA and an action list we can present to our internal compliance committee on Friday.

What we need: a short timeline, a root cause summary at a customer level, outstanding mitigations and commitments (owners + ETA), and suggested verification steps we can run on our side.

Attaching the traces we pulled; happy to hop on a quick call if it speeds things up.

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Platform Reliability
Stellar Bank

Subject: Internal: quick sync — Stellar Bank traces and deliverables

Marissa/Hannah/Irene — forwarding Elena’s traces. Quick summary from initial triage:
- Impact window: 2028-05-03 02:15–03:05 UTC; tokenization latency increased and ~12% of requests returned 503s under our autoscaling threshold.
- Early signs point to a KV-cache eviction storm on a subset of dedicated pools serving long-tail customer keys; eviction churn caused higher downstream CPU and serialization retries.

Customer asks: EOD May 5 customer-facing RCA + verification playbook; May 7 walkthrough call.

Proposed deliverables and tentative owners:
1) Customer RCA PDF (Grace lead) — include non-sensitive technical appendix and timeline — due EOD May 5.
2) Short-term mitigations (Marissa lead) — increased cache grace window and biasing cache misses, temporary routing to warm pools — implement by May 5 18:00 UTC.
3) Long-term fix (Hannah lead) — adjust eviction heuristics + metric alerts for eviction-rate; rollout plan by May 12.
4) Verification playbook (Irene lead) — step-by-step checks + dashboard queries for Stellar Ops; deliverable with checklist.

I’ll draft the RCA and coordinate internal review. Please acknowledge and update ETA if any of these are unrealistic.

— Grace

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@stellarbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, SupportOps <supportops@stellarbank.com>
Date: 2028-05-05T17:58:00-07:00
Subject: [RCA draft] May 3 tokenization latency spike — customer summary & actions (draft)

Elena / Stellar team — please find the draft RCA attached and pasted below in brief. Thank you for your patience while we completed the investigation. We welcome any immediate feedback; we plan to finalize the packet after your review.

Attachment: 0504-stellarbank-rca-draft.pdf (customer-facing summary + technical appendix)

Executive summary:
- Impact: Elevated tokenization latency and intermittent 503s for a subset of Stellar Bank requests during 2028-05-03 02:15–03:05 UTC (UTC).
- Root cause (short): A cascade of KV-cache evictions in a dedicated pool for certain long-tail keys caused repeated recomputation and CPU contention on inference workers, resulting in increased tail latency and a small fraction of requests failing when requests timed out during retries.
- Why it happened: A latent regression in our cache eviction scoring caused aggressive eviction under a particular client traffic pattern (high fan-in, infrequent reuse). This regression was introduced as part of a cache heuristic change deployed April 27 (config id: cache-v4.1).

Timeline (customer-facing):
- 2028-04-27 15:20 UTC: cache-v4.1 heuristic deployed broadly to dedicated pools.
- 2028-05-03 02:12 UTC: Stellar high-priority flow traffic increases (scheduled job overlap); cache miss rate begins to climb for pool P-03.
- 2028-05-03 02:15–03:05 UTC: Eviction churn spikes; worker CPU and serialization retries rise; tokenization latency elevated; ~12% of requests returned 503s or timed out.
- 2028-05-03 03:06 UTC: Temporary routing to warm pools applied; failures decreased and latency returned to baseline by 03:20 UTC.

Immediate actions completed (done May 3):
- Rerouted affected traffic to warm pools (Marissa) — stabilized within 15 minutes.
- Rolled back cache-v4.1 for dedicated pools serving long-tail keys (Hannah) — eliminated eviction churn.
- Increased health-check sensitivity and added temporary alert for eviction-rate spikes (Marissa).

Planned next steps (owners & ETA):
- Short-term (by 2028-05-05 18:00 UTC): Bias caching to prefer sticky entries for affected workloads; extra grace window to reduce churn (Marissa).
- Medium-term (by 2028-05-12): Update eviction scoring to incorporate reuse probability and add synthetic load tests for fan-in patterns (Hannah).
- Verification playbook (by 2028-05-06): Step-by-step checks and dashboard queries for Stellar Ops + a shared checklist (Irene). Deliverable attached on May 6.

Verification (what Stellar can run):
- Query: eviction_rate/pool=P-03 over 1m, 5m; ensure no spikes during scheduled jobs.
- Synthetic: run a short fan-in job (link in playbook) and compare miss curves.
- Acceptance: no eviction bursts > 5x baseline in 1h window across P-03 after rollout.

Compensation/credits: Our account team will follow up separately per contract.

Next meeting: Proposed May 7 16:00 UTC (45m) to walk through the playbook and schedule verification window.

Please let me know any redactions needed; we can strip config ids or internal metric names for compliance.

Thanks,
Grace
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Grace — thank you for the thorough draft. A few quick asks from our compliance and SRE teams:
1) Can you remove internal metric names in the customer PDF (ok to keep high-level metric values).
2) For the verification playbook, please include exact PromQL snippets we can paste into our dashboards.
3) Please include a short section describing how you will prevent a recurrence at the engineering/process level (not just config fixes).

We’ll review and aim to confirm by EOD May 6. We also accept the May 7 walkthrough; I’ll send a calendar invite.

— Elena
